gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-lexend-giga: Amadeus stretches its words wide and bold across the line. Lexend Giga follows in a plain sans, flat-lined and generously tracked, giving those broad headings a spacious, modern partner underneath.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads like it was drawn with a single nib, its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Amadeus above it stays bold and commanding.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads big and friendly, with curves that never thin and a wide-mouthed c. Amadeus, commanding and stretched out, sits over a body that is sans-serif yet matches its generous width.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera draws its sans-serif letters like a plotter pen, every curve open and each letter standing well apart. And Amadeus brings the opposite energy, stretched wide and bold, which is what makes the pairing memorable.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta cuts its strokes like ribbon of constant width, with tall small letters spaced far apart. Amadeus, by contrast, is the one for commanding, wide-stretched display; Lexend Zetta is the sans that keeps text approachable.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-montserrat-alterna: Amadeus stretches out wide and commanding, with round letters that carry no tilted stress at all. Montserrat Alternates, a contemporary sans, handles the quieter text work.
gen-dafont-arkhip-crimson-pro: Crimson Pro is a refined serif with close-packed lines and a gentle thick-and-thin cadence. Arkhip is its opposite up top, geometric and unmodulated, so a slightly larger body size would let the serif breathe.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-recia: Sharp and authoritative, Recia keeps its modulation light, visible only up close, while its openings stay generous. But Arkhip has no swell at all where curves turn, so the heading looks geometric and the body looks carefully cut.
gen-dafont-aurulent-sans-fs-bespoke-seri: Bespoke Serif reads dignified and authoritative, its thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones. And Aurulent Sans gives it an organic, clean partner whose terminals point outward.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-gambetta: Azonix keeps its capitals barely above its lowercase. Azonix commands the headline with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk, while Gambetta, a graceful serif, supplies the bookish warmth of shifting stroke weight.
